standard_prerequisites.name: Product of a simplicial object with the standard simplex
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cylinder U times the standard 1-simplex, computed degreewise, together with the two end inclusions and the projection (the author's lemma lemma-back-to-U, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the description of the maps e_0, e_1 and pi used in the statement and the proof (source lines 4834-4836, 4846-4869).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy between morphisms of simplicial objects
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two morphisms are homotopic when there is a family of degreewise maps satisfying the face and degeneracy identities of a homotopy.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof constructs such families explicitly, using maxima of simplex coordinates for the first and minima for the second (source lines 4850-4870).

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite coproducts in the base category
standard_prerequisites.statement: The category admits finite coproducts, which is what allows the standard simplices and their products with U to be formed degreewise.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis that makes the cylinder and the maps exist (source lines 4832-4833).

core_obligations: Verify the projection identities: using the description of the maps given by the retained lemma, compute componentwise that the projection composed with each end inclusion is the identity of U (source lines 4846-4855).

Construct the first homotopy: define in each degree a map from the cylinder into the next degree of the cylinder by a formula using the maximum of the simplex coordinates, and check the face and degeneracy identities so that it is a homotopy from the identity to the composite through the first end inclusion (source lines 4855-4869).

Obtain the second homotopy: repeat the construction replacing the maximum by the minimum to get the homotopy from the identity to the composite through the second end inclusion (source lines 4869-4870).

proof_roadmap.step: Compute the projection identities from the description of the maps.
Define the maximum formula and verify it is a homotopy to the first composite.
Replace maximum by minimum to obtain the second homotopy.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-contractible at source lines 4830-4844, three statements about the cylinder U times the standard 1-simplex: the projection composed with either of the two end inclusions is the identity, and the identity of the cylinder is homotopic both to the composite through the first end inclusion and to the composite through the second. The proof at source lines 4846-4871 has to write down the homotopies explicitly. It uses the description of the relevant maps supplied by the author's lemma on the pair (U, the standard 1-simplex), defines in each degree a map into the next degree of the cylinder by a formula involving the maximum of the simplex coordinates, verifies the face and degeneracy identities that make it a homotopy, and then notes that the same construction with the minimum instead of the maximum gives the second homotopy. The first statement is a componentwise computation with the same description. The statement lists the conclusions and none of the formulas. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
